'''Yann Ulrich Stéphane Lasme'''<ref name="full name">{{cite web | url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/51817/sid/4524/tid/284/tid2//_/2005_FIBA_Africa_Championship_for_Men/index.html | archive-url=https://archive.today/20130122231320/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/51817/sid/4524/tid/284/tid2//_/2005_FIBA_Africa_Championship_for_Men/index.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=January 22, 2013 | title=13 – Yann Ulrich Stephane Lasme | publisher=Archive.fiba.com | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> (born December 17, 1982) is a Gabonese former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst|University of Massachusetts]] (UMass), with the [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass Minutemen]],<ref name=bio>{{cite web | url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lasme_stephane00.html | title=Player Bio: Stephane Lasme :: Men's Basketball | publisher=Umassathletics.com | access-date=December 18, 2011 | archive-date=July 29, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120729223140/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lasme_stephane00.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> and he was selected by the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the second round, 46th overall, in the [[2007 NBA draft]].<ref name=drafted>{{cite web | url=http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062907aab.html | title=Stephane Lasme Of UMass Selected By Golden State In The NBA Draft | publisher=Atlantic10.com | date=June 29, 2007 | access-date=December 18, 2011 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327133453/http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062907aab.html | archive-date=March 27, 2012 }}</ref> In 2016 Stephane won the EuroCup Championship and earned the Finals MVP award, as well as, an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection in [[2013–14 Euroleague|2014]] and won the [[EuroLeague Best Defender]] award in [[2012–13 Euroleague|2013]], among others.

==Early career==
On December 17, 1982, Lasme was born in [[Port-Gentil]], [[Gabon]], to Onanga Liliane. He was brought up in [[Port-Gentil]], [[Gabon]], his father being an oil company engineer. His mother, Liliane, was an economist. Lasme knew how to speak French and his native language of [[Myene language|Myene]] in his childhood, but learned some English through high school classes.<ref name=outofafrica>{{cite web|last1=Chimelis|first1=Ron|title=Springfield Republican: Out Of Africa|url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/012906aaa.html|website=UMassAthletics.com|publisher=[[The Republican (Springfield, Massachusetts)|Springfield Republican]]|access-date=10 March 2015}}</ref>

Lasme grew up loving [[Association football|soccer]], but began playing basketball at 14,<ref name=about>{{cite web|title=About Us|url=http://www.stephanelasme.com/bio.html|website=StephaneLasme.com|access-date=10 March 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402091159/http://www.stephanelasme.com/bio.html|archive-date=2 April 2015}}</ref> when he was introduced to his school's coach. When asked why he started playing the game, Lasme said, "I was growing faster than the other kids my age." One media report stated that he nailed a basketball hoop to a tree at age 15 and estimated the official NBA requirement of 10 feet, but instead put it 12 feet above the ground. He said, "I had a rim put in at my house. It was higher than 10 feet, though." His favorite players as a child were [[Scottie Pippen]] and [[Michael Jordan]], whom he used to watch on television by sneaking out of bed at night. He also grew up as a fan of [[Marcus Camby]].

Lasme competed for Aveley Club [[Port-Gentil]], a youth club that was designed to be an after-school program. He attended high school at Léon M'ba in his native [[Gabon]]<ref name=bio /> and was called up by Arimbi Nkolo, head coach of his country's [[Gabon national basketball team|national team]]. While at Léon M'ba, whose basketball team competed in the African High School Federation, he played under Ebolo Firmin. Lasme also played for Capo Libreville in the [[2002 FIBA Africa Basketball Club Championship]].<ref name=about />

==College career==
In February 2003 Lasme moved to the United States. Lasme's cousin, Serge Lapeby gave him a home in [[Boston]]. He helped him adjust to the new environment, saying, "He had to learn the culture, the language, the colder weather—that was a bit of a challenge—and the lifestyle." He was forced to compete in a gymnasium, as he arrived in the United States in the winter, and played in [[Emmanuel College (Massachusetts)|Emmanuel College]]. Lapeby tried to recruit Lasme to play for the school's team, and succeeded, but it did not offer athletic scholarships as an [[NCAA Division III]] college.<ref name=outofafrica />

Lasme subsequently enrolled in [[Emmanuel College (Massachusetts)|Emmanuel College]], primarily for its [[English as a second or foreign language|ESL]] program. He began playing basketball for the college and attracted the attention of many [[NCAA Division I]] programs. Lasme's performance in the Eastern Invitational All-Star Game, which took place in New Jersey, was most noted.<ref name=about /> The game was attended by [[UMass Minutemen basketball|Massachusetts Minutemen basketball]] coach [[Steve Lappas]], who was searching for potential recruits.<ref name=outofafrica />

Lappas was impressed by Lasme's raw skills and offered him a scholarship to play for the Minutemen. He signed an institutional financial aid agreement to compete with Massachusetts for the [[2003–04 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2003–04 season]] and was eligible to participate in the winter.<ref name=minutemen>{{cite web | url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/072103aab.html | title=Minutemen Land Foreign Standout | publisher=Umassathletics.com | date=July 21, 2003 | access-date=December 18, 2011 | archive-date=May 28, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120528214050/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/072103aab.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> When the move was made official, the coach said, "We are excited to have Stephane join our program. We believe that he is a quality student and athlete. It is very exciting to find someone of his caliber at this point in time, and we feel he will be a very good addition to our program."<ref name=minutemen />

===Freshman===
On November 9, 2003, Lasme made his first appearance in a Massachusetts uniform in an exhibition game against the [[Harlem Globetrotters]]. He finished with 1 point and 5 turnovers in 9 minutes of playing time, as the Minutemen fell to Harlem, 68–77.<ref>{{cite web|title=Globetrotters 77, Massachusetts 68|url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/110903aaa.html|website=UMassAthletics.com|access-date=10 March 2015|date=November 9, 2003|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402101340/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/110903aaa.html|archive-date=2 April 2015}}</ref> He competed in another exhibition game on November 14 against the Playaz basketball club, but was awarded 22 minutes on the court.<ref>{{cite web|title=Massachusetts 95, Playaz 87|url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/111403aaa.html|website=UMassAthletics.com|access-date=10 March 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402091415/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/111403aaa.html|archive-date=2 April 2015}}</ref> In his official collegiate debut, a win over [[St. Francis Brooklyn Terriers men's basketball|St. Francis (NY)]], Lasme contributed 6 points and 6 rebounds off the bench.<ref name=freshmangamelogs>{{cite web|title=Stephane Lasme Game Logs|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Stephane-Lasme/GameLogs/375/NCAA/2004|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=10 March 2015}}</ref> He grabbed 13 rebounds in a quarterfinals game of the Preseason [[National Invitational Tournament]] vs [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]], the first time he recorded double-digits in any major statistical category at the collegiate level. He also had four blocked shots,<ref name=freshmangamelogs /> as UMass fell, 50–90.<ref>{{cite web|title=Minutemen Fall To Texas Tech, 90-50|url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112103aaa.html|website=UMassAthletics.com|access-date=10 March 2015}}</ref> Lasme scored a season-high 13 points on February 8, 2004, vs [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]]. He was awarded his first-ever start with the Minutemen on January 18, 2004, against [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]], but scored no points.<ref name=freshmangamelogs /> He was named the winner of [[UMass Minutemen basketball|Massachusetts]]' Jack Leaman Defensive Award at the end of the season, ranking second in the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] in blocked shots. Lasme finished the year with averages of 3.2 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.8 blocks.<ref name=bio />

===Sophomore===
As a sophomore, he started all 28 games for the [[UMass Minutemen basketball|Minutemen]], and again finished as the league's second-leading shot blocker.

===Junior===
Lasme continued his progression during his junior year. He started 27 of the team's 28 games (Senior Day being the exception), scored in double figures 15 times, and finished the year with a 10.5 average. Lasme was two blocks short of a triple-double against [[Saint Peter's Peacocks basketball|St. Peter's]] on December 27, 2005, with 21 points, 14 rebounds and 8 blocks. By the end of the season, Lasme blocked a total of 108 shots, an average of 3.9 per game, good for third-highest in the nation. The A-10 honored Lasme with their Defensive Player of the Year award.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030606aaa.html | title=Lasme Named A-10 Defensive Player Of Year | publisher=Umassathletics.com | date=March 6, 2006 | access-date=December 18, 2011 | archive-date=May 28, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120528214055/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030606aaa.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Senior===
Lasme's senior year at UMass was filled with personal accomplishments, records, and team success. He was named an AP Honorable Mention All-American,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032607aaa.html | title=Lasme Named AP Honorable Mention All-American | publisher=Umassathletics.com | date=March 26, 2007 | access-date=December 18, 2011 | archive-date=June 21, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130621125637/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032607aaa.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> the Atlantic 10 Player of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030507aac.html | title=Lasme Named A-10 Player Of The Year & Defensive Player Of The Year | publisher=Umassathletics.com | date=March 5, 2007 | access-date=December 18, 2011 | archive-date=May 28, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120528214105/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030507aac.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> He ranked first in the league in blocks and rebounding, and second in field goal percentage. He scored more than 20 points on four occasions, grabbed 10 or more rebounds on 17 occasions, and 10 or more blocks on four occasions. During the season, Lasme averaged 13.5 points, 9.5 rebounds, and 5.1 blocks per game, and led the Minutemen into the [[2007 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], the team's first post-season play since the 1999–2000 season.

In the 2006–07 season, Lasme tied an NCAA record with four [[triple-double]]s in a single season, joining [[Jason Kidd]] (1994 at Cal) and [[Michael Anderson (basketball)|Michael Anderson]] (1986 at Drexel). While Kidd and Anderson accomplished the feat by achieving double figures in scoring, rebounds, and assists, Lasme's triple-doubles are in scoring, rebounds and blocks. His four triple-doubles were:

* vs. St. Francis on November 22 (19 pts, 10 reb, 11 blocks);
* vs. George Washington on January 10 (23 pts, 15 reb, 11 blocks);
* vs. Rhode Island on February 8 (18 pts, 12 reb, 11 blocks) and
* vs. La Salle on February 28 (17 pts, 10 reb, 10 blocks).<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032607aaa.html | title=Stephane Lasme Of UMass Garners AP Honorable Mention All-America Honors | publisher=Atlantic10.com | date=March 26, 2007 | access-date=December 18, 2011 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327133508/http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032607aaa.html | archive-date=March 27, 2012 }}</ref>

Also in 2006–07 Lasme set new UMass records for career blocked shots (399), single season blocked shots (168), and blocks per game (11), passing [[Marcus Camby]] on all three lists.

==Professional career==
In June 2007, Lasme was selected in the second round, 46th overall, in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]], using the pick they got from the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]] in exchange for [[Clifford Robinson (basketball, born 1966)|Clifford Robinson]].<ref name=drafted /><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062807aab.html | title=Lasme Selected By Golden State Warriors With 46th Pick In NBA Draft | publisher=Umassathletics.com | date=June 28, 2007 | access-date=December 18, 2011 | archive-date=May 28, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120528214110/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062807aab.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> He made his [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] debut on November 8, playing only 3.8 seconds of game time in the Warriors 120–115 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap/_/id/271108009/dallas-mavericks-vs-golden-state-warriors | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107153305/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap/_/id/271108009/dallas-mavericks-vs-golden-state-warriors | url-status=dead | archive-date=November 7, 2012 | title=Nowitzki comes up big as Mavs hold off Warriors | publisher=Espn.go.com | date=November 8, 2007 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/110907aaa.html | title=Lasme Makes NBA Debut For Warriors On Thursday Night | publisher=Umassathletics.com | date=November 9, 2007 | access-date=December 18, 2011 | archive-date=May 28, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120528214130/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/110907aaa.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> On November 17, Lasme was waived by the Warriors.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=3117739 | title=Warriors sign C DJ Mbenga, waive draft pick Lasme | publisher=[[ESPN]] | date=November 18, 2007 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> Later that month, he was signed by the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]]'s [[South Bay Lakers|Los Angeles D-Fenders]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.us/dleague/losangeles/karl_071128.html | title=D-Fenders sign forward Stephane Lasme, waive forward Marcus White | publisher=Nba.us | date=November 28, 2007 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/112907aaa.html | title=Lasme signs with Los Angeles D-Fenders | publisher=Umassathletics.com | date=November 29, 2007 | access-date=December 18, 2011 | archive-date=May 28, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120528214143/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/112907aaa.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

On March 21, 2008, Lasme was signed to a ten-day contract with the [[Miami Heat]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=3608623 | title=Los Angeles D-Fender Stephane Lasme Earns Gatorade Call-Up To Miami Heat | publisher=Oursportscentral.com | date=March 21, 2008 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> whose roster had been depleted by injuries. He later signed for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041108aag.html | title=Lasme Signed For Year By Heat; Named D-League Co-Def. Player Of Year | publisher=Umassathletics.com | date=April 11, 2008 | access-date=December 18, 2011 | archive-date=May 28, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120528214206/http://www.umassathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041108aag.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> In 15 games (four starts), he averaged 5.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.5 blocks and 20.2 minutes.

In September 2008, Lasme signed with the [[Adriatic League]] champions [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]], for the 2008–09 season.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/35612/180 | title=Partizan lands Stephane Lasme | publisher=Euroleague.net | date=September 22, 2008 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> After the opening three games in [[EuroLeague]], he was ranked second in both blocks and rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/37851/179 | title=Stephane Lasme, Partizan Belgrade | publisher=Euroleague.net | date=November 11, 2008 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> Lasme finished the season well, averaging 10.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks per game, 25.5 minutes a contest, after Partizan's strong showing that ended in the quarterfinals with a loss to [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]]. He was instrumental in helping the team to another [[ABA League|regional ABA championship]], with 11.3 points per game. He also won [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian national championship]] and the Serbian [[Radivoj Korać Cup]] titles with Partizan.

In July 2009, Lasme signed with the [[Israeli Basketball Super League|Israeli League]] club [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], along with [[Alan Anderson (basketball)|Alan Anderson]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/54900/3694 | title=MACCABI: Lasme & Anderson come aboard | publisher=Euroleague.net | date=July 25, 2009 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> On June 8, 2010, Maccabi announced that they had released Lasme, after a foot injury had limited his playing time towards the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://thehoop.blogspot.com/2010/06/maccabi-ta-released-stephane-lasme.html | title=Maccabi TA released Stephane Lasme | publisher=Thehoop.blogspot.com | date=June 8, 2010 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> In 20 games of EuroLeague play, he averaged 6.5 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 1.4 blocks per game in 18.5 minutes per game. Lasme then signed a two-year contract with the [[Russian Professional Basketball League|Russian League]] club [[BC Spartak Saint Petersburg|Spartak Saint Petersburg]] in July 2010.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/73977/3735/item | archive-url=https://archive.today/20130122093617/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/73977/3735/item | url-status=dead | archive-date=January 22, 2013 | title=Spartak St. Petersburg tabs Stephane Lasme | publisher=Eurocupbasketball.com | date=July 24, 2010 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> However, he was released in September, due to some administrative problems that he had in the United States.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/75255/3735/item | archive-url=https://archive.today/20130122204300/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/75255/3735/item | url-status=dead | archive-date=January 22, 2013 | title=Spartak St. Petersburg, Lasme part ways | publisher=Eurocupbasketball.com | date=September 6, 2010 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref>

Lasme was invited to join the [[Boston Celtics]] for their 2010 training camp.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/basketball/celtics/view/20101011stephane_lasme_grabbing_docs_attention/ | title=Stephane Lasme grabbing Doc's attention | publisher=Bostonherald.com | date=October 11, 2010 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> However, he was waived on October 20.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.masslive.com/mywideworld/index.ssf/2010/10/lasme_waived_by_the_boston_celtics.html | title=Stephane Lasme waived by the Boston Celtics | publisher=Masslive.com | date=October 20, 2010 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> Subsequently, Lasme joined the [[Maine Red Claws]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA D-League]], an affiliate of the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4677689/red-claws-add-nine-through-draft | title=Red Claws add nine through draft | publisher=Espn.go.com | date=November 2, 2010 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> However, Lasme fractured his foot just 2 minutes into the team's preseason opener against the [[Springfield Armor]], and immediately underwent surgery.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4678172/lasme-out-indefinitely-after-surgery | title=Lasme out 'indefinitely' after surgery | publisher=Espn.go.com | date=November 18, 2010 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> After recovering, he returned to action in March 2011.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4681546/lasme-returns-to-red-claws | title=Lasme returns to Red Claws | publisher=Espn.go.com | date=March 10, 2011 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref>

In August 2011, Lasme returned to Europe and signed with the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] newcomers [[Obradoiro CAB]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/30397/obradoiro_cab_lands_stephane_lasme.html | title=Obradoiro CAB lands Stephane Lasme | publisher=Sportando.net | date=August 12, 2011 | access-date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> On July 5, 2012, the Boston Celtics announced that Lasme was added to their roster for the 2012 [[Orlando Pro Summer League]] and the [[2012 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.weei.com/sports/boston/this-just-in/21211731/rookies-williams-cs-summer-league-roster | title=Sean Williams on C's summer league roster | publisher=Weei.com | date=July 5, 2012 | access-date=July 9, 2012}}</ref>

On September 29, 2012, Lasme signed a one-year contract with the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] club [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos Athens]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/greece/44220/panathinaikos-announced-stephane-lasme.html | title=Panathinaikos announced Stephane Lasme | publisher=Sportando.net | date=September 29, 2012 | access-date=September 29, 2012}}</ref> He was named the [[EuroLeague Best Defender]] for the [[2012–13 Euroleague]] season. He averaged 1.86 blocks and 6.14 rebounds per game, while his team allowed 69.8 points per game, thus displaying the second best team defense in the league.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/112932/180 | title=Best Defender Trophy winner: Stephane Lasme, Panathinaikos Athens | publisher=Euroleague.net | date=May 2, 2013 | access-date=May 2, 2013}}</ref> Also, Lasme earned the [[Greek Basket League MVP]] award, as well as the [[Greek Basket League Best Defender|Greek League Best Defender]] award for the 2012–13 season.

On July 1, 2013, Lasme renewed his contract with Panathinaikos for two more years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=4467|title = Ανανέωση με Λάσμε| date=July 2013 }}</ref> In May 2014, he was named to the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] of the EuroLeague.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=2013-14 All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/136869|work=Euroleague.net|access-date=9 May 2014}}</ref> He also earned the Greek League Best Defender award and was named to the [[Greek Basket League Pentad|Greek League Best Five]] for the 2013–14 season. Panathinaikos decided to exercise an "opt out" clause in his contract for the upcoming 2014–15 season, on 12 June 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=23071 |title=Ανακοίνωση ΚΑΕ Παναθηναϊκός |access-date=June 12, 2014 |archive-date=July 14, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714164327/http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=23071 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On June 22, 2014, he signed a two-year contract with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes Istanbul]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Anadolu Efes lands defensive ace Lasme|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/138126|website=euroleague.net|access-date=24 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Anadolu Efes officially sign Stephane Lasme|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/123687/anadolu-efes-officially-sign-stephane-lasme.html|access-date=June 22, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=June 22, 2014}}</ref> On July 29, 2015, he signed with [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Galatasaray adds experienced center Lasme|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/68gwgvamgjog5sgp|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150731211416/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/68gwgvamgjog5sgp|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 31, 2015|access-date=29 July 2015|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=29 July 2015}}</ref> Lasme was instrumental in winning the Eurocup title 2015–16, and earned the [[EuroCup Basketball Finals MVP|Eurocup Finals MVP award]].<ref name=":1">{{cite news|title=Lasme named Eurocup Finals MVP|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/6ugoctmyavp89ji9/lasme-named-eurocup-finals-mvp|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160502120744/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/6ugoctmyavp89ji9/lasme-named-eurocup-finals-mvp|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 2, 2016|access-date=January 23, 2018|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=April 27, 2016}}</ref> On August 29, 2016, Lasme was suspended for one year after failing a doping test.<ref>{{cite web|title=Galatasaray'ın eski oyuncusu Stephane Lasme'ye dopingten 1 yıl men!|url=https://www.haberturk.com/spor/basketbol/haber/1289440-galatasarayin-eski-oyuncusu-stephane-lasmeye-dopingten-1-yil-men|website=haberturk.com|access-date=August 30, 2016|language=tr-TR|date=August 29, 2016}}</ref>

On February 10, 2017, Lasme was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]] of the NBA Development League.<ref>{{cite news|title=Legends Acquire Stéphane Lasme|url=http://texas.dleague.nba.com/news/legends-acquire-stephane-lasme/|access-date=February 11, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2017}}</ref>

On July 13, 2017, Lasme signed with Russian club [[BC UNICS|UNICS]] for the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Unics adds 7DAYS EuroCup champ Lasme|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/7xxl6k7aotmnoecs|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170716020249/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/7xxl6k7aotmnoecs|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 16, 2017|access-date=July 13, 2017|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=July 13, 2017}}</ref>

On June 27, 2018, Lasme officially returned to [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] after four years, signing a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Lasme, Panathinaikos together again|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8u57cu3i8aglawh5/lasme-panathinaikos-together-again|access-date=July 14, 2018|work=EuroLeague.net|date=June 27, 2018}}</ref>

In September 2022, Lasme returned from his retirement after four years when he joined the Gabonese club [[Espoir Basket Club|Espoir]] to play for them in the [[2023 BAL qualification|2023 BAL qualification tournament]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2022-09-17 |title=Gabon-Basketball : Stéphane Lasme un renfort de taille pour Espoir BC |url=https://agencedepressepanafricaine.com/gabon-basketball-stephane-lasme-un-renfort-de-taille-pour-espoir-bc/ |access-date=2022-10-02 |website=Agence de Presse Panafricaine |language=fr-FR}}</ref> Despite training with the team for a month, he did not join Espoir for their games in [[Yaoundé]], [[Cameroon]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beyeme |first=Willy Eyi |date=2022-10-10 |title=Basketball-Zone 4/Espoir BC à l'Africa League à Yaoundé sans Stéphane Lasme |url=https://gabonallsport.com/index.php/2022/10/10/basketball-zone-4-espoir-bc-a-lafrica-league-a-yaounde-sans-stephane-lasme/ |access-date=2022-10-13 |website=Gabonallsport |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

==National team career==
Lasme played with the senior [[Gabonese national basketball team|Gabonese national team]] at the [[2005 FIBA Africa Championship]], averaging 11.7 points, 10.1 rebounds, and 3 blocks per game, in seven games played.<ref name="full name" />

He played his second continental tournament at [[AfroBasket 2015]] and averaged 11.2 points and 6.8 rebounds per game.<ref name="full name" />
